children.name: Aegithalos
children.description: Tiny tail-heavy birds that move through woodland in chattering flocks. They build one of the most elaborate nests in European ornithology — an oval elastic cocoon of moss and lichen woven with spider silk and lined with hundreds of feathers, expandable as the chicks grow. In hard winters they huddle together for warmth at roost.

children.name: Aegithalos caudatus
children.description: The long-tailed tit or long-tailed bushtit is a common bird species belonging to the bushtit family found throughout Eurasia. An insectivore, it inhabits deciduous and mixed woodlands as well as scrub, heathland, farmland, parks and gardens. The plumage of this small long-tailed bird is predominantly black and white with varying amounts of pink and grey.

children.name: Aegithalos glaucogularis
children.description: The silver-throated bushtit or silver-throated tit (Aegithalos glaucogularis) is a species of passerine bird in the family Aegithalidae, widespread throughout the temperate forests of Central, East and parts of North and Western China. The bird's native habitats are mainly along the middle/lower Yangtze and Yellow River basins, although there is also a small southwestern habitat extension in Yunnan along the Lancang valley within the Hengduan Mountains. It has two recognized subspecies.

children.name: Aegithalos concinnus
children.description: The black-throated bushtit (Aegithalos concinnus), also known as the black-throated tit, is a very small passerine bird in the family Aegithalidae.

children.name: Aegithalos iouschistos
children.description: The black-browed bushtit (Aegithalos iouschistos), also known as the black-browed tit or rufous-fronted bushtit, is a species of bird in the family Aegithalidae. It is found in mid-southern China and sporadically in Myanmar. Its natural habitats are boreal forests and temperate forests. The subspecies A. B. Sharpei (Burmese tit) of western Burma and A. I. Bonvaloti of southern China have sometimes been treated as separate species.

children.name: Aegithalos bonvaloti
children.description: The black-browed bushtit (Aegithalos iouschistos), also known as the black-browed tit or rufous-fronted bushtit, is a species of bird in the family Aegithalidae. It is found in mid-southern China and sporadically in Myanmar. Its natural habitats are boreal forests and temperate forests. The subspecies A. B. Sharpei (Burmese tit) of western Burma and A. I. Bonvaloti of southern China have sometimes been treated as separate species.

children.name: Aegithalos fuliginosus
children.description: The sooty bushtit (Aegithalos fuliginosus), also known as the sooty tit, white-necklaced tit or white-necklaced bushtit, is a small passerine bird in the bushtit family Aegithalidae.

children.name: Aegithalos niveogularis
children.description: The white-throated bushtit (Aegithalos niveogularis), also known as the white-throated tit, is a species of bird in the family Aegithalidae. It is found in India, Nepal, and Pakistan. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Aegithalos leucogenys
children.description: The white-cheeked bushtit (Aegithalos leucogenys), also known as the white-cheeked tit, is a species of bird in the family Aegithalidae. It is found in Afghanistan, India, and Pakistan.

children.name: Aegithalos sharpei

Bonvaloti of southern China have sometimes been treated as separate species.

children.name: Psaltria
children.description: A monotypic genus for the pygmy bushtit, the smallest member of the family, endemic to the mountains of Java.

children.name: Psaltria exilis
children.description: The pygmy bushtit (Aegithalos exilis), also called the pygmy tit, is the smallest species of passerine bird.

children.name: Psaltriparus
children.description: A monotypic genus for the American bushtit, the only member of the family in the New World.

children.name: Psaltriparus minimus
children.description: The American bushtit, or simply bushtit (Psaltriparus minimus), is a social songbird belonging to the monotypic genus Psaltriparus.

children.name: Leptopoecile
children.description: The tit-warblers, brilliantly coloured small birds of high Central Asian mountains, washed in violet, blue, and lilac.

children.name: Leptopoecile sophiae
children.description: The white-browed tit-warbler (Leptopoecile sophiae) is a species of bird in the family Aegithalidae. The species was first described by Nikolai Severtzov in 1873. It is resident in the Tian Shan and central China as well as in the Himalayas where it is mainly found in winter. Its natural habitat is boreal forests.

children.name: Leptopoecile elegans
children.description:
The crested tit-warbler (Leptopoecile elegans) is a species of bird in the family Aegithalidae. It is found in China and possibly India. Its natural habitat is boreal forest. It generally has a red hint to it and a bit of blue on, or near, its wings. The tail is of an emerald green colour.
This species is considered monotypic, although it was previously divided into two subspecies: the type subspecies and the subspecies meissneri, which was lumped with elegans in 2022.
